- 
+ # Prerequisites Before Building
+ 
+ Before you can test and apply this Nix configuration, you need to:
+ 
+ ## 1. Install Nix
+ 
+ Choose one of the following:
+ 
+ ### Option A: Lix Installer (Recommended)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Option B: Official Nix Installer
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ curl -L https://nixos.org/nix/install | sh
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ After installation, restart your terminal or source the Nix profile.
+ 
+ ## 2. Update Secrets Repository URL
+ 
+ The secrets repository URL in &#96;flake.nix&#96; is currently set to a placeholder:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ url = "git+ssh://git@github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/nix-secrets.git";
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **You must update this to your own secrets repository** before building:
+ 
+ 1. Create a private GitHub repository for your secrets (e.g., &#96;yourusername/nix-secrets&#96;)
+ 2. Update the URL in &#96;flake.nix&#96; line 31
+ 3. Set up your SSH keys to access the repository
+ 
+ Alternatively, if you don't have a secrets repo yet, you can:
+ - Comment out the secrets input in &#96;flake.nix&#96;
+ - Comment out the secrets usage in &#96;modules/darwin/secrets.nix&#96;
+ 
+ ## 3. Make Apps Executable
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd nixos-config
+ find apps/$(uname -m | sed 's/arm64/aarch64/')-darwin -type f \( -name apply -o -name build -o -name build-switch -o -name create-keys -o -name copy-keys -o -name check-keys -o -name rollback \) -exec chmod +x {} \;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## 4. Test Build
+ 
+ Once Nix is installed and secrets repo is configured:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd nixos-config
+ nix run .#build
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will build the configuration without applying it, which is safe to test.
+ 
+ ## 5. Apply Configuration
+ 
+ After a successful build:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ nix run .#build-switch
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will apply the configuration to your system.
+ 
+ ## Notes
+ 
+ - The configuration has been adapted for user "me" (username)
+ - Git config has been set to: Aaron Culich &lt;aculich@gmail.com&gt;
+ - Editor has been changed from Emacs to vim
+ - All tools from the current toolchain have been added
+ 
```

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash

- 
+ # Large Packages - Excluded from Initial Installation
+ 
+ This document lists large packages that are **not** included in the initial Nix configuration to keep installation fast. These can be added later when needed.
+ 
+ ## Excluded Packages
+ 
+ ### Mobile Development IDEs
+ 
+ #### Xcode (~10-15 GB)
+ - **Status**: Not in Nix config
+ - **Why excluded**: Very large download, long installation time (20-30 minutes)
+ - **How to add later**: 
+   - Add to &#96;modules/darwin/home-manager.nix&#96; in &#96;masApps&#96;:
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+     masApps = {
+       "Xcode" = 497799835;
+       # ... other apps
+     };
+   - Or install manually: &#96;mas install 497799835&#96;
+ - **Note**: &#96;xcodes&#96; (Xcode version manager) is included - it's small and useful for managing Xcode versions
+ 
+ #### Android Studio (~1-2 GB)
+ - **Status**: Not in Nix config
+ - **Why excluded**: Large download, 5-10 minute installation
+ - **How to add later**:
+   - Add to &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;:
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+     [
+       # ... other casks
+       "android-studio"
+     ]
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;
+   - Or install manually: &#96;brew install --cask android-studio&#96;
+ 
+ ### LaTeX Distribution
+ 
+ #### MacTeX (~4-5 GB)
+ - **Status**: Not in Nix config
+ - **Why excluded**: Very large, 10-15 minute download, often fails due to unreliable CTAN mirrors
+ - **How to add later**:
+   - Add to &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;:
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+     [
+       # ... other casks
+       "mactex-no-gui"  # Minimal version without GUI apps
+       # Or: "mactex"  # Full version with GUI apps
+     ]
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;
+   - Or install manually: &#96;brew install --cask mactex-no-gui&#96;
+ - **Note**: If download fails, install manually from https://www.tug.org/mactex/
+ 
+ ### Data Science Tools
+ 
+ #### R (~500 MB + compilation time)
+ - **Status**: Not in Nix config
+ - **Why excluded**: Large package, requires compilation (5-10 minutes)
+ - **How to add later**:
+   - Add to &#96;modules/shared/packages.nix&#96;:
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+     with pkgs; [
+       # ... other packages
+       r
+     ]
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;
+   - Or install via Homebrew: &#96;brew install r&#96;
+   - Or use pixi (already included) for R environments
+ 
+ #### RStudio (~200 MB)
+ - **Status**: Not in Nix config
+ - **Why excluded**: Medium size, requires R to be useful
+ - **How to add later**:
+   - Add to &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;:
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+     [
+       # ... other casks
+       "rstudio"
+     ]
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;
+   - Or install manually: &#96;brew install --cask rstudio&#96;
+ - **Note**: Requires R to be installed first
+ 
+ ### Container Runtimes
+ 
+ #### OrbStack (~500 MB)
+ - **Status**: Not in Nix config (using colima instead)
+ - **Why excluded**: Medium size, colima is already included as alternative
+ - **Current choice**: &#96;colima&#96; is included (smaller, open-source alternative)
+ - **How to add later** (if preferred):
+   - Add to &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;:
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+     [
+       # ... other casks
+       "orbstack"
+     ]
+     &#96;&#96;&#96;
+   - Note: Choose either colima OR orbstack, not both
+ 
+ ## Installation Strategy
+ 
+ ### Recommended Approach
+ 
+ 1. **Initial install**: Use the optimized Nix config (fast, complete-enough)
+ 2. **Add large packages as needed**: Install when you actually need them
+ 3. **Use Homebrew for large packages**: Some large packages are easier to manage via Homebrew:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    # Install Xcode via Mac App Store
+    mas install 497799835
+    
+    # Install Android Studio
+    brew install --cask android-studio
+    
+    # Install R and RStudio
+    brew install r
+    brew install --cask rstudio
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Why This Approach?
+ 
+ - **Faster initial setup**: Get a working environment quickly
+ - **Flexibility**: Add large packages only when needed
+ - **Easier updates**: Large packages can be updated independently
+ - **Less disk space**: Don't install what you don't use
+ 
+ ## Size Reference
+ 
+ | Package | Size | Install Time |
+ |---------|------|--------------|
+ | Xcode | ~10-15 GB | 20-30 min |
+ | MacTeX | ~4-5 GB | 10-15 min |
+ | Android Studio | ~1-2 GB | 5-10 min |
+ | R | ~500 MB | 5-10 min (compile) |
+ | RStudio | ~200 MB | 2-3 min |
+ | OrbStack | ~500 MB | 2-3 min |
+ 
+ ## Notes
+ 
+ - All essential development tools are included in the initial config
+ - Large IDEs (Xcode, Android Studio) are typically installed once and updated infrequently
+ - Data science tools (R, RStudio) can be added when starting data science projects
+ - LaTeX is only needed for document preparation - install when needed
+ 
```

@@ -1,1 +1,510 @@
- 
+ # Nix Configuration Guide
+ 
+ This guide explains how the Nix configuration works, how to customize it, and where to add your own configurations.
+ 
+ ## Table of Contents
+ 
+ 1. [Overview](#overview)
+ 2. [Flake Structure](#flake-structure)
+ 3. [Module System](#module-system)
+ 4. [Home Manager](#home-manager)
+ 5. [nix-darwin](#nix-darwin)
+ 6. [Homebrew Integration](#homebrew-integration)
+ 7. [Secrets Management](#secrets-management)
+ 8. [Customization Points](#customization-points)
+ 9. [Common Tasks](#common-tasks)
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ 
+ This configuration uses **Nix Flakes** to manage a declarative macOS development environment. Everything is defined in code and can be reproduced on any machine.
+ 
+ ### Key Technologies
+ 
+ - **Nix Flakes** - Reproducible builds with locked dependencies
+ - **nix-darwin** - System-level macOS configuration
+ - **home-manager** - User environment and dotfiles
+ - **nix-homebrew** - Declarative Homebrew management
+ - **agenix** - Encrypted secrets management
+ 
+ ## Flake Structure
+ 
+ ### &#96;flake.nix&#96; - Entry Point
+ 
+ The &#96;flake.nix&#96; file is the entry point that orchestrates everything:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ {
+   inputs = {
+     # External dependencies
+     nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
+     home-manager.url = "github:nix-community/home-manager";
+     darwin.url = "github:LnL7/nix-darwin/master";
+     # ... more inputs
+   };
+   
+   outputs = { self, ... } @inputs: {
+     # Build outputs
+     darwinConfigurations = { ... };
+     apps = { ... };
+   };
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Key sections:**
+ - **&#96;inputs&#96;** - External dependencies (nixpkgs, home-manager, etc.)
+ - **&#96;outputs&#96;** - What the flake produces (configurations, apps, etc.)
+ - **&#96;user&#96;** - Your username (set to "me" in this config)
+ 
+ ### Flake Apps
+ 
+ The flake provides convenient commands:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ nix run .#build          # Build configuration without applying
+ nix run .#build-switch   # Build and apply configuration
+ nix run .#apply          # Alias for build-switch
+ nix run .#rollback       # Rollback to previous generation
+ nix run .#clean          # Clean old generations
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Module System
+ 
+ The configuration is organized into **modules** that can be composed together.
+ 
+ ### Directory Structure
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ nixos-config/
+ ├── flake.nix              # Entry point
+ ├── hosts/                  # System-level configurations
+ │   ├── darwin/            # macOS host config
+ │   └── nixos/             # Linux host config
+ └── modules/               # Reusable modules
+     ├── darwin/            # macOS-specific modules
+     │   ├── casks.nix     # GUI applications (Homebrew casks)
+     │   ├── packages.nix  # macOS-specific CLI tools
+     │   ├── home-manager.nix  # macOS home-manager config
+     │   └── secrets.nix   # macOS secrets
+     ├── nixos/             # Linux-specific modules
+     └── shared/            # Cross-platform modules
+         ├── packages.nix  # Shared CLI tools
+         ├── home-manager.nix  # Shared shell/git/editor configs
+         └── files.nix     # Shared dotfiles
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### How Modules Work
+ 
+ Modules are imported in &#96;hosts/darwin/default.nix&#96;:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ {
+   imports = [
+     ../../modules/darwin/secrets.nix
+     ../../modules/darwin/home-manager.nix
+     ../../modules/shared
+     agenix.darwinModules.default
+   ];
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Each module can:
+ - Define system packages
+ - Configure system settings
+ - Import other modules
+ - Set environment variables
+ 
+ ## Home Manager
+ 
+ **Home Manager** manages your user environment: dotfiles, shell configs, git settings, etc.
+ 
+ ### Configuration Location
+ 
+ - **macOS**: &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96; + &#96;modules/darwin/home-manager.nix&#96;
+ - **Linux**: &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96; + &#96;modules/nixos/home-manager.nix&#96;
+ 
+ ### What Home Manager Manages
+ 
+ 1. **Shell Configuration** (&#96;zsh&#96;)
+    - Plugins (powerlevel10k)
+    - Aliases
+    - Environment variables
+    - PATH modifications
+ 
+ 2. **Git Configuration** (&#96;git&#96;)
+    - User name and email
+    - Default branch
+    - Editor settings
+    - GPG signing
+ 
+ 3. **Editor Configuration** (&#96;vim&#96;)
+    - Plugins
+    - Key bindings
+    - Color schemes
+ 
+ 4. **SSH Configuration** (&#96;ssh&#96;)
+    - Host entries
+    - Identity files
+    - Includes external config files
+ 
+ 5. **Dotfiles** (&#96;home.file&#96;)
+    - Any file in your home directory
+    - Managed declaratively
+ 
+ ### Example: Adding a Dotfile
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ # In modules/shared/files.nix
+ {
+   ".config/myapp/config.yml".source = ./myapp-config.yml;
+   
+   ".local/bin/myscript" = {
+     executable = true;
+     text = ''
+       #!/bin/bash
+       echo "Hello from Nix!"
+     '';
+   };
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## nix-darwin
+ 
+ **nix-darwin** manages system-level macOS configuration.
+ 
+ ### Configuration Location
+ 
+ &#96;hosts/darwin/default.nix&#96; - System-level settings
+ 
+ ### What nix-darwin Manages
+ 
+ 1. **System Packages** (&#96;environment.systemPackages&#96;)
+    - Packages available system-wide
+    - Emacs daemon
+    - agenix tools
+ 
+ 2. **System Settings** (&#96;system.defaults&#96;)
+    - Dock configuration
+    - Finder settings
+    - Trackpad settings
+    - Keyboard repeat rates
+ 
+ 3. **Launch Agents** (&#96;launchd.user.agents&#96;)
+    - Background services
+    - Emacs daemon
+ 
+ 4. **Nix Settings** (&#96;nix.settings&#96;)
+    - Cache configuration
+    - Garbage collection
+    - Trusted users
+ 
+ ### Example: Changing Dock Settings
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ # In hosts/darwin/default.nix
+ system.defaults.dock = {
+   autohide = true;        # Auto-hide dock
+   show-recents = false;   # Don't show recent apps
+   tilesize = 48;          # Icon size
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Homebrew Integration
+ 
+ **nix-homebrew** manages Homebrew declaratively through Nix.
+ 
+ ### How It Works
+ 
+ 1. **Casks** (GUI apps) - Defined in &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;
+ 2. **Formulas** (CLI tools) - Can be added to packages.nix or managed via Homebrew
+ 3. **Mac App Store Apps** - Defined in &#96;modules/darwin/home-manager.nix&#96; &#96;masApps&#96;
+ 
+ ### Adding a Cask (GUI App)
+ 
+ Edit &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ _:
+ [
+   # ... existing casks
+   "my-new-app"
+ ]
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Then rebuild: &#96;nix run .#build-switch&#96;
+ 
+ ### Adding a Mac App Store App
+ 
+ 1. Find the app ID:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    nix shell nixpkgs#mas
+    mas search "App Name"
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. Add to &#96;modules/darwin/home-manager.nix&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+    masApps = {
+      "App Name" = 123456789;
+    };
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Third-Party Taps
+ 
+ By default, &#96;mutableTaps = false&#96; in &#96;flake.nix&#96;, which means third-party taps cannot be declared in Nix.
+ 
+ **To use third-party taps:**
+ - Install manually: &#96;brew install tapname/formula&#96;
+ - Or change &#96;mutableTaps = true&#96; in &#96;flake.nix&#96; (allows manual tap management)
+ 
+ ## Secrets Management
+ 
+ **agenix** manages encrypted secrets using age encryption.
+ 
+ ### How It Works
+ 
+ 1. **Secrets Repository** - Private GitHub repo (configured in &#96;flake.nix&#96;)
+ 2. **Encryption** - Secrets encrypted with your SSH public key
+ 3. **Decryption** - Automatically decrypted at build time using your SSH private key
+ 
+ ### Configuration
+ 
+ **Secrets repo URL**: &#96;flake.nix&#96; (line 33)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ secrets = {
+   url = "git+ssh://git@github.com/aculich/nix-secrets.git";
+   flake = false;
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Secrets definition**: &#96;modules/darwin/secrets.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ age.secrets."github-ssh-key" = {
+   symlink = true;
+   path = "/Users/me/.ssh/id_github";
+   file = "${secrets}/github-ssh-key.age";
+   mode = "600";
+   owner = "me";
+   group = "staff";
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Adding a New Secret
+ 
+ 1. **Create encrypted secret** in your secrets repo:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    cd ~/nix-secrets
+    age -r "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..." -o mysecret.age &lt; /path/to/plaintext
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Define in secrets.nix**:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+    age.secrets."mysecret" = {
+      file = "${secrets}/mysecret.age";
+      path = "/Users/me/.config/myapp/secret";
+      mode = "600";
+    };
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Reference in config** (if needed):
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+    environment.variables.MY_SECRET = config.age.secrets.mysecret.path;
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Customization Points
+ 
+ ### Where to Add Your Config
+ 
+ #### 1. CLI Tools and Libraries
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/packages.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ with pkgs; [
+   # ... existing packages
+   my-new-tool
+ ]
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### 2. GUI Applications
+ **File**: &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ _:
+ [
+   # ... existing casks
+   "my-new-app"
+ ]
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### 3. Shell Configuration
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ zsh = {
+   initContent = lib.mkBefore ''
+     # Your custom shell code
+     alias myalias='command'
+   '';
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### 4. Git Configuration
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ git = {
+   settings = {
+     user.name = "Your Name";
+     user.email = "your@email.com";
+     # ... other git settings
+   };
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### 5. System Settings (macOS)
+ **File**: &#96;hosts/darwin/default.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ system.defaults = {
+   # Dock, Finder, Trackpad settings
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### 6. Dotfiles
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/files.nix&#96; or &#96;modules/darwin/files.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ {
+   ".config/myapp/config".source = ./my-config-file;
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### 7. Environment Variables
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ home.sessionVariables = {
+   MY_VAR = "value";
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Common Tasks
+ 
+ ### Adding a New Package
+ 
+ 1. **Find the package name**:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    nix search nixpkgs package-name
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Add to appropriate file**:
+    - CLI tool → &#96;modules/shared/packages.nix&#96;
+    - macOS-only tool → &#96;modules/darwin/packages.nix&#96;
+    - GUI app → &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Rebuild**:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    nix run .#build-switch
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Changing Shell Prompt
+ 
+ Current: &#96;powerlevel10k&#96;
+ 
+ To switch to &#96;starship&#96;:
+ 
+ 1. **Add starship** to &#96;modules/shared/packages.nix&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+    starship
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Update** &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+    starship = {
+      enable = true;
+      settings = {
+        # Your starship config
+      };
+    };
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Remove powerlevel10k** from zsh plugins
+ 
+ ### Changing Default Editor
+ 
+ Current: &#96;vim&#96;
+ 
+ To change:
+ 
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ # In zsh.initContent
+ export EDITOR="your-editor"
+ export VISUAL="your-editor"
+ 
+ # In git.settings
+ core.editor = "your-editor";
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Adding a Custom Script
+ 
+ **File**: &#96;modules/shared/files.nix&#96; or &#96;modules/darwin/files.nix&#96;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ {
+   ".local/bin/myscript" = {
+     executable = true;
+     text = ''
+       #!/bin/bash
+       # Your script here
+     '';
+   };
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Updating Packages
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Update all flake inputs
+ nix flake update
+ 
+ # Update specific input
+ nix flake update nixpkgs
+ 
+ # Rebuild with updates
+ nix run .#build-switch
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Troubleshooting
+ 
+ **Build fails:**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Show full error trace
+ nix run .#build -- --show-trace
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Something broke after switch:**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Rollback to previous generation
+ nix run .#rollback
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Clean up old generations:**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ nix run .#clean
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## File Reference
+ 
+ | File | Purpose |
+ |------|---------|
+ | &#96;flake.nix&#96; | Entry point, inputs, outputs |
+ | &#96;hosts/darwin/default.nix&#96; | System-level macOS config |
+ | &#96;modules/shared/packages.nix&#96; | Cross-platform CLI tools |
+ | &#96;modules/darwin/packages.nix&#96; | macOS-specific CLI tools |
+ | &#96;modules/darwin/casks.nix&#96; | GUI applications |
+ | &#96;modules/shared/home-manager.nix&#96; | Shell, git, editor configs |
+ | &#96;modules/darwin/home-manager.nix&#96; | macOS home-manager setup |
+ | &#96;modules/darwin/secrets.nix&#96; | Encrypted secrets |
+ | &#96;modules/shared/files.nix&#96; | Shared dotfiles |
+ | &#96;modules/darwin/files.nix&#96; | macOS-specific dotfiles |
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ 1. **Customize for your needs** - Add/remove packages, change settings
+ 2. **Set up secrets** - Create your secrets repository and add encrypted secrets
+ 3. **Build and test** - Run &#96;nix run .#build&#96; to test before applying
+ 4. **Apply configuration** - Run &#96;nix run .#build-switch&#96; when ready
+ 
+ For more details, see the main [README.md](README.md).
+ 
```

- 
+ # Toolchain Integration Notes
+ 
+ This document notes patterns and features from the current Homebrew-based toolchain that might be useful to incorporate into the Nix configuration.
+ 
+ ## Recent Toolchain Evolution
+ 
+ ### Key Additions (Recent Commits)
+ 
+ 1. **Reset Strategy System** (&#96;docs/RESET_STRATEGY.md&#96;)
+    - Soft/hard/nuclear reset options
+    - Machine identity detection (Workhorse vs SideQuest)
+    - Pre-reset inventory system
+    - **Nix Note**: Nix already provides rollback capabilities, but reset strategies could be useful for complete environment resets
+ 
+ 2. **Configuration Scanning** (&#96;scripts/scan-dotfiles.sh&#96;, &#96;scripts/scan-applications.sh&#96;)
+    - Automated discovery of dotfiles and applications
+    - Classification as "builder tools" vs "house tools"
+    - **Nix Note**: Nix manages dotfiles declaratively, but scanning could help identify what to migrate
+ 
+ 3. **Companion Repository Management** (&#96;scripts/sync-companions.sh&#96;)
+    - Self-contained companion repos in &#96;companions/&#96; directory
+    - Sync and management scripts
+    - **Nix Note**: Could be managed via Nix flakes or kept as separate repos
+ 
+ 4. **Time Tracking** (built into install scripts)
+    - Tracks installation times
+    - Logs to &#96;~/.bootstrap-times.log&#96;
+    - **Nix Note**: Could add timing to Nix build process
+ 
+ 5. **Security Scanning Infrastructure**
+    - gitleaks, trufflehog, detect-secrets
+    - Pre-commit hooks
+    - **Nix Note**: Already included in Nix packages!
+ 
+ 6. **Machine Identity** (&#96;scripts/machine-identity.sh&#96;)
+    - Detects machine type (Workhorse, SideQuest, etc.)
+    - Conditional configuration based on machine
+    - **Nix Note**: Could use Nix's system detection or environment variables
+ 
+ ## Integration Opportunities
+ 
+ ### What to Keep in Homebrew
+ 
+ - **Large packages** (Xcode, Android Studio, MacTeX) - Better managed via Homebrew/MAS
+ - **Frequently updated apps** - Some apps update faster via Homebrew
+ - **Third-party taps** - Easier to manage manually
+ 
+ ### What to Move to Nix
+ 
+ - **CLI tools** - Already in Nix packages
+ - **Dotfiles** - Managed by home-manager
+ - **Shell configuration** - Managed by home-manager
+ - **System settings** - Managed by nix-darwin
+ 
+ ### What to Keep Separate
+ 
+ - **Companion repositories** - Keep as separate git repos
+ - **Project-specific configs** - Keep in projects (&#96;.envrc&#96;, &#96;.tool-versions&#96;)
+ - **Application data** - Keep in &#96;~/Library/Application Support/&#96;
+ 
+ ## Patterns to Consider
+ 
+ ### 1. Machine-Specific Configuration
+ 
+ **Current approach**: &#96;scripts/machine-identity.sh&#96; detects machine type
+ 
+ **Nix approach**: Use environment variables or system detection:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ # In hosts/darwin/default.nix
+ let
+   machineType = builtins.getEnv "MACHINE_TYPE" or "default";
+ in
+ {
+   # Conditional config based on machine type
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 2. Time Tracking
+ 
+ **Current approach**: Built into install scripts
+ 
+ **Nix approach**: Could add to flake apps:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;nix
+ "build-switch-timed" = {
+   type = "app";
+   program = "${writeScript "build-switch-timed" ''
+     #!/bin/bash
+     start=$(date +%s)
+     nix run .#build-switch
+     end=$(date +%s)
+     echo "Build took $((end - start)) seconds"
+   ''}/bin/build-switch-timed";
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 3. Configuration Scanning
+ 
+ **Current approach**: &#96;scripts/scan-dotfiles.sh&#96; discovers configs
+ 
+ **Nix approach**: Not needed - everything is declarative, but could create a script to:
+ - List all managed dotfiles
+ - Compare with system state
+ - Identify drift
+ 
+ ### 4. Reset Strategies
+ 
+ **Current approach**: &#96;scripts/hard-reset.sh&#96;, &#96;scripts/soft-reset.sh&#96;
+ 
+ **Nix approach**: 
+ - **Soft reset**: &#96;nix run .#rollback&#96;
+ - **Hard reset**: &#96;nix run .#clean&#96; + rebuild
+ - **Nuclear reset**: Uninstall Nix + reinstall
+ 
+ ## Migration Path
+ 
+ ### Phase 1: Core Nix Setup (Current)
+ - ✅ Username and git config updated
+ - ✅ Secrets repo created
+ - ✅ Large packages excluded
+ - ✅ Tools from toolchain added
+ 
+ ### Phase 2: Dotfile Migration
+ - Migrate shell configs to home-manager
+ - Migrate editor configs to home-manager
+ - Migrate tool configs (tmux, etc.) to home-manager
+ 
+ ### Phase 3: Operational Tools
+ - Add reset/rollback scripts as flake apps
+ - Add configuration validation scripts
+ - Add time tracking to builds
+ 
+ ### Phase 4: Advanced Features
+ - Machine-specific configurations
+ - Conditional package installation
+ - Integration with companion repos
+ 
+ ## Notes
+ 
+ - **Companion repos**: Keep as separate repos, sync via scripts
+ - **Project configs**: Keep in projects, not in Nix
+ - **Application data**: Keep in standard macOS locations
+ - **Large packages**: Install via Homebrew when needed
+ - **Security tools**: Already in Nix packages
+ 
+ ## References
+ 
+ - &#96;docs/CONFIGURATION_INVENTORY.md&#96; - What configs exist
+ - &#96;docs/REPOSITORY_STORY.md&#96; - Toolchain evolution
+ - &#96;docs/RESET_STRATEGY.md&#96; - Reset strategies
+ - &#96;scripts/&#96; - Operational scripts
+

- 
+ # Nix Installation Checklist
+ 
+ Use this checklist before and during Nix configuration installation.
+ 
+ ## Pre-Installation
+ 
+ ### ✅ Prerequisites
+ 
+ - [x] GitHub CLI authenticated (&#96;gh auth status&#96;)
+ - [x] Secrets repository created (&#96;aculich/nix-secrets&#96;)
+ - [x] Secrets repo URL updated in &#96;flake.nix&#96;
+ - [x] Username updated to "me" in all config files
+ - [x] Git config updated (Aaron Culich &lt;aculich@gmail.com&gt;)
+ - [x] Large packages excluded (see &#96;LARGE_PACKAGES.md&#96;)
+ - [x] Configuration guide created (&#96;CONFIGURATION_GUIDE.md&#96;)
+ 
+ ### 📋 Before Installing Nix
+ 
+ - [ ] **Backup important data** (if this is a production machine)
+ - [ ] **Review configuration** - Check &#96;flake.nix&#96; and modules
+ - [ ] **Check disk space** - Ensure at least 10GB free
+ - [ ] **Review large packages** - Understand what's excluded (see &#96;LARGE_PACKAGES.md&#96;)
+ 
+ ## Installation Steps
+ 
+ ### 1. Install Nix
+ 
+ Choose one:
+ 
+ **Option A: Lix (Recommended)**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Option B: Official Nix**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ curl -L https://nixos.org/nix/install | sh
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ After installation:
+ - Restart terminal or source the Nix profile
+ - Verify: &#96;nix --version&#96;
+ 
+ ### 2. Set Up Secrets Repository
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Clone your secrets repository
+ git clone git@github.com:aculich/nix-secrets.git ~/nix-secrets
+ 
+ # Create basic secrets.nix structure
+ cd ~/nix-secrets
+ # (You'll need to set up age keys and encrypt secrets)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Note**: The secrets repo is required for the build. If you don't have secrets yet, you can:
+ - Create an empty &#96;secrets.nix&#96; file
+ - Or comment out secrets usage temporarily
+ 
+ ### 3. Make Apps Executable
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config
+ find apps/$(uname -m | sed 's/arm64/aarch64/')-darwin -type f \
+   \( -name apply -o -name build -o -name build-switch -o \
+      -name create-keys -o -name copy-keys -o -name check-keys -o \
+      -name rollback \) -exec chmod +x {} \;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 4. Test Build (Dry Run)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config
+ nix run .#build
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Expected**: Build completes without errors
+ 
+ **If errors occur**:
+ - Check secrets repository is accessible
+ - Verify SSH keys are set up for secrets repo
+ - Review error messages and fix issues
+ 
+ ### 5. Apply Configuration
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ nix run .#build-switch
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Expected**: 
+ - Configuration builds successfully
+ - System switches to new configuration
+ - All packages install
+ - Homebrew casks install
+ 
+ **Time estimate**: 10-30 minutes depending on:
+ - Number of packages
+ - Network speed
+ - System performance
+ 
+ ### 6. Verify Installation
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Check Nix packages
+ which git
+ which gh
+ which mise
+ which uv
+ 
+ # Check Homebrew casks
+ brew list --cask | head -10
+ 
+ # Check system settings
+ defaults read com.apple.dock
+ 
+ # Check home-manager
+ home-manager generations
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Post-Installation
+ 
+ ### ✅ Verification Checklist
+ 
+ - [ ] Nix packages are in PATH
+ - [ ] Homebrew casks are installed
+ - [ ] Shell configuration loaded (check &#96;~/.zshrc&#96;)
+ - [ ] Git config correct (&#96;git config user.name&#96;)
+ - [ ] Editor works (&#96;vim --version&#96;)
+ - [ ] Dotfiles in place (check &#96;~/.config/&#96;)
+ 
+ ### 🔧 Common Issues
+ 
+ **Issue**: Packages not in PATH
+ - **Solution**: Restart terminal or source &#96;~/.zshrc&#96;
+ 
+ **Issue**: Homebrew casks not installing
+ - **Solution**: Check &#96;brew doctor&#96;, ensure Homebrew is working
+ 
+ **Issue**: Secrets not decrypting
+ - **Solution**: Check SSH keys, verify secrets repo access
+ 
+ **Issue**: Build fails with "path does not exist"
+ - **Solution**: Run &#96;nix flake update&#96; to refresh inputs
+ 
+ ### 📝 Next Steps
+ 
+ 1. **Customize configuration** - See &#96;CONFIGURATION_GUIDE.md&#96;
+ 2. **Add large packages** - See &#96;LARGE_PACKAGES.md&#96; when needed
+ 3. **Set up secrets** - Add encrypted secrets to &#96;~/nix-secrets&#96;
+ 4. **Review toolchain integration** - See &#96;TOOLCHAIN_INTEGRATION_NOTES.md&#96;
+ 
+ ## Rollback Plan
+ 
+ If something goes wrong:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Rollback to previous generation
+ nix run .#rollback
+ 
+ # Or manually
+ darwin-rebuild switch --flake .#aarch64-darwin
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Resources

- 
+ # Git Workflow for nixos-config
+ 
+ This document explains how we manage this repository, which is adapted from &#96;natea/nixos-config&#96;.
+ 
+ ## Remote Setup
+ 
+ We maintain two remotes:
+ 
+ - **&#96;origin&#96;** - Your own repository (&#96;aculich/nixos-config&#96;)
+   - Push your customizations here
+   - This is your "source of truth"
+ 
+ - **&#96;nate&#96;** - Nate's original repository (&#96;natea/nixos-config&#96;)
+   - Pull updates from here
+   - Keep this as a reference
+ 
+ ## Workflow
+ 
+ ### Viewing Remotes
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ git remote -v
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Pulling Updates from Nate
+ 
+ When Nate updates his config and you want to incorporate changes:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Fetch updates from Nate's repo
+ git fetch nate
+ 
+ # See what changed
+ git log main..nate/main
+ 
+ # Create a branch to merge updates
+ git checkout -b merge-nate-updates
+ git merge nate/main
+ 
+ # Resolve any conflicts, then merge to main
+ git checkout main
+ git merge merge-nate-updates
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Pushing Your Changes
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Push to your own repo
+ git push origin main
+ 
+ # Or push a feature branch
+ git push origin feature-branch-name
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Creating a Branch from Nate's Latest
+ 
+ If you want to start fresh from Nate's latest:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Fetch latest from Nate
+ git fetch nate
+ 
+ # Create a new branch from Nate's main
+ git checkout -b fresh-from-nate nate/main
+ 
+ # Make your customizations
+ # ... edit files ...
+ 
+ # Commit and push
+ git commit -am "feat: my customizations"
+ git push origin fresh-from-nate
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Grafting Other Repos
+ 
+ This same pattern works for other repos you want to track:
+ 
+ ### Adding Another Upstream Repo
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Add someone else's nix config as a remote
+ git remote add other-person https://github.com/other-person/nixos-config
+ 
+ # Fetch their updates
+ git fetch other-person
+ 
+ # Create a branch from their main
+ git checkout -b other-person-variant other-person/main
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Keeping Multiple Variants
+ 
+ You can maintain multiple branches, each based on different upstreams:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Branch from Nate's
+ git checkout -b nate-variant nate/main
+ 
+ # Branch from another person's
+ git checkout -b other-variant other-person/main
+ 
+ # Your customized version
+ git checkout main
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Best Practices
+ 
+ 1. **Keep &#96;main&#96; as your customized version** - This is what you use day-to-day
+ 2. **Pull from &#96;nate&#96; periodically** - Stay up to date with improvements
+ 3. **Merge carefully** - Review changes before merging to avoid breaking your setup
+ 4. **Document customizations** - Keep notes on what you changed and why
+ 5. **Test before merging** - Always test merged changes before pushing
+ 
+ ## Alternative: Git Subtree
+ 
+ If you want to include this as a subdirectory in &#96;toolchain-2026&#96;:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # From toolchain-2026 root
+ git subtree add --prefix=nixos-config nate main --squash
+ 
+ # Pull updates later
+ git subtree pull --prefix=nixos-config nate main --squash
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This keeps it as part of your main repo but allows pulling updates.
+ 
+ ## Alternative: Git Submodule
+ 
+ If you want to reference it as a submodule in &#96;toolchain-2026&#96;:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # From toolchain-2026 root
+ git submodule add https://github.com/aculich/nixos-config.git nixos-config
+ 
+ # Update later
+ git submodule update --remote nixos-config
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This keeps it as a separate repo but linked to your main repo.
+ 
+ ## Current Setup
+ 
+ Right now, &#96;nixos-config&#96; is a **standalone repository** with:
+ - Your customizations on &#96;main&#96; branch
+ - Pushed to &#96;aculich/nixos-config&#96;
+ - Tracking &#96;natea/nixos-config&#96; for updates
+ 
+ This gives you:
+ - ✅ Full control over your config
+ - ✅ Ability to pull updates from Nate
+ - ✅ Clean separation from toolchain-2026
+ - ✅ Easy to share or fork
+ 
```

+ # Quick Start - Install Nix Configuration
+ 
+ ## Step 1: Install Nix (Manual - Requires Sudo)
+ 
+ Run this command in your terminal (it will prompt for your password):
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Or use the official Nix installer:**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ curl -L https://nixos.org/nix/install | sh
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ After installation:
+ - **Restart your terminal** or run: &#96;source ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh&#96;
+ - Verify: &#96;nix --version&#96;
+ 
+ ## Step 2: Set Up Secrets Repository
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Clone your secrets repository (if not already done)
+ git clone git@github.com:aculich/nix-secrets.git ~/nix-secrets
+ 
+ # Create a basic secrets.nix file (if empty)
+ cd ~/nix-secrets
+ cat &gt; secrets.nix &lt;&lt; 'EOF'
+ let
+   # Add your SSH public key here
+   your_key = "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... your@email.com";
+ in
+ {
+   # Define which keys can decrypt each secret
+   # "github-ssh-key.age".publicKeys = [ your_key ];
+ }
+ EOF
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Note**: For now, you can create an empty &#96;secrets.nix&#96; file. We'll set up actual secrets later.
+ 
+ ## Step 3: Test Build
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config
+ 
+ # Test build (doesn't apply, just builds)
+ nix run .#build
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ If this succeeds, you're ready to apply!
+ 
+ ## Step 4: Apply Configuration
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Build and apply the configuration
+ nix run .#build-switch
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will:
+ - Build the configuration
+ - Install all Nix packages
+ - Install all Homebrew casks
+ - Configure your system
+ - Set up dotfiles
+ 
+ **Time estimate**: 10-30 minutes
+ 
+ ## Step 5: Verify
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Check packages are installed
+ which git
+ which gh
+ which mise
+ which uv
+ 
+ # Check Homebrew casks
+ brew list --cask | head -10
+ 
+ # Check home-manager
+ home-manager generations
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### Build Fails with "path does not exist"
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Update flake inputs
+ nix flake update
+ nix run .#build
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Secrets Repository Not Found
+ - Make sure you've cloned: &#96;git clone git@github.com:aculich/nix-secrets.git ~/nix-secrets&#96;
+ - Or temporarily comment out secrets in &#96;flake.nix&#96; and &#96;modules/darwin/secrets.nix&#96;
+ 
+ ### Need to Rollback
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ nix run .#rollback
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ - See &#96;CONFIGURATION_GUIDE.md&#96; for customization
+ - See &#96;LARGE_PACKAGES.md&#96; for adding large packages later
+ - See &#96;GIT_WORKFLOW.md&#96; for managing updates from Nate's repo
+ 
```

+ #!/usr/bin/env bash
+ # Lix installer with automatic yes answers and verbose logging
+ 
+ set -euo pipefail
+ 
+ SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &amp;&amp; pwd)"
+ LOG_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../logs"
+ mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
+ 
+ LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/lix-install-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
+ 
+ echo "==========================================" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "Lix Installer - $(date)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "Log file: $LOG_FILE" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "==========================================" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo ""
+ 
+ # Function to log and display
+ log() {
+     echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ }
+ 
+ log "Starting Lix installation..."
+ log "This will require your sudo password"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Install with automatic yes answers
+ # The installer will prompt for:
+ # 1. Enable flakes? (Y)
+ # 2. Proceed? (Y)
+ # We pipe "yes" to answer all prompts, and use sudo -S to read password from stdin if needed
+ # But since we can't securely pass password, user will need to enter it
+ 
+ log "Downloading and running Lix installer..."
+ log "You will be prompted for your sudo password"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Use yes to answer all prompts, but sudo will still ask for password interactively
+ # We capture all output to the log file
+ (
+     echo "Y"  # Enable flakes
+     echo "Y"  # Proceed
+ ) | \
+ while IFS= read -r line; do
+     echo "$line" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ done
+ 
+ # Alternative: Use expect if available (more reliable)
+ if command -v expect &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+     log "Using expect for automated installation..."
+     expect &lt;&lt; 'EXPECT_SCRIPT' | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ set timeout 300
+ spawn bash -c "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install"
+ 
+ # Wait for prompts and answer them
+ expect {
+     "Enable flakes?" {
+         send "Y\r"
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     "Proceed?" {
+         send "Y\r"
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     "Password:" {
+         # User will need to enter password manually
+         interact
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     "sudo" {
+         # If sudo prompt appears, let user handle it
+         interact
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     eof
+ }
+ EXPECT_SCRIPT
+ else
+     log "expect not available, using manual method..."
+     log "Please answer 'Y' to all prompts when they appear"
+     curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ fi
+ 
+ log ""
+ log "Installation complete!"
+ log "Log saved to: $LOG_FILE"
+ log ""
+ log "Next steps:"
+ log "1. Restart your terminal or run: source ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh"
+ log "2. Verify: nix --version"
+ log "3. Test build: cd $SCRIPT_DIR &amp;&amp; nix run .#build"
+ 
```

+ #!/usr/bin/env bash
+ # Lix installer using expect for full automation with logging
+ 
+ set -euo pipefail
+ 
+ SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &amp;&amp; pwd)"
+ LOG_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../logs"
+ mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
+ 
+ LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/lix-install-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
+ 
+ echo "==========================================" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "Lix Installer (Automated) - $(date)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "Log file: $LOG_FILE" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "==========================================" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo ""
+ 
+ # Check for expect
+ if ! command -v expect &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+     echo "Error: expect is required for automated installation"
+     echo "Install with: brew install expect"
+     exit 1
+ fi
+ 
+ # Create expect script
+ expect &lt;&lt; 'EXPECT_SCRIPT' 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ set timeout 600
+ set log_file [open "$env(LOG_FILE)" a]
+ 
+ # Spawn the installer
+ spawn bash -c "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install"
+ 
+ # Enable verbose output
+ log_user 1
+ exp_internal 0
+ 
+ # Handle all prompts
+ expect {
+     -re "Enable flakes\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+         puts $log_file "[AUTO] Answering 'Y' to enable flakes"
+         send "Y\r"
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "Proceed\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+         puts $log_file "[AUTO] Answering 'Y' to proceed"
+         send "Y\r"
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "(Password|password):" {
+         puts $log_file "[PROMPT] Sudo password required - user will enter manually"
+         interact {
+             \r { send "\r" }
+         }
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "sudo.*password" {
+         puts $log_file "[PROMPT] Sudo password required - user will enter manually"
+         interact {
+             \r { send "\r" }
+         }
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     timeout {
+         puts $log_file "[ERROR] Timeout waiting for prompt"
+         exit 1
+     }
+     eof {
+         puts $log_file "[SUCCESS] Installation complete"
+         close $log_file
+     }
+ }
+ EXPECT_SCRIPT
+ 
+ EXIT_CODE=$?
+ 
+ echo ""
+ echo "==========================================" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then
+     echo "Installation completed successfully!" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ else
+     echo "Installation may have encountered issues (exit code: $EXIT_CODE)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ fi
+ echo "Full log: $LOG_FILE" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ echo "==========================================" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ 
+ exit $EXIT_CODE
+ 
```

+ #!/usr/bin/env bash
+ # Automated Lix installer - answers yes to all prompts, logs everything
+ # You'll need to enter sudo password when prompted
+ 
+ set -euo pipefail
+ 
+ SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &amp;&amp; pwd)"
+ LOG_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../logs"
+ mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
+ 
+ LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/lix-install-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
+ 
+ echo "=========================================="
+ echo "Lix Automated Installer"
+ echo "Log file: $LOG_FILE"
+ echo "=========================================="
+ echo ""
+ echo "This will:"
+ echo "  - Answer 'Y' to enable flakes"
+ echo "  - Answer 'Y' to proceed with installation"
+ echo "  - Log all output to: $LOG_FILE"
+ echo ""
+ echo "You will be prompted for your sudo password"
+ echo "Press Enter to continue, or Ctrl+C to cancel..."
+ read -r
+ 
+ # Use 'yes' to answer all prompts with 'Y'
+ # Log everything to file and display on screen
+ yes | \
+ curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | \
+ sh -s -- install 2&gt;&amp;1 | \
+ tee "$LOG_FILE"
+ 
+ INSTALL_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[2]}
+ 
+ echo ""
+ echo "=========================================="
+ if [ $INSTALL_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
+     echo "✓ Installation completed successfully!"
+ else
+     echo "⚠ Installation exited with code: $INSTALL_EXIT"
+     echo "  Check the log file for details"
+ fi
+ echo "=========================================="
+ echo ""
+ echo "Full log: $LOG_FILE"
+ echo ""
+ echo "Next steps:"
+ echo "1. Restart terminal or run:"
+ echo "   source ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh"
+ echo ""
+ echo "2. Verify installation:"
+ echo "   nix --version"
+ echo ""
+ echo "3. View installation log:"
+ echo "   tail -f $LOG_FILE"
+ echo "   or"
+ echo "   cat $LOG_FILE"
+ 
+ exit $INSTALL_EXIT
+ 
```

+ #!/usr/bin/env bash
+ # Fully automated Lix installer with explain-then-yes and comprehensive logging
+ # Captures system state before/after and generates a "nix story" document
+ 
+ set -euo pipefail
+ 
+ SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &amp;&amp; pwd)"
+ LOG_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../logs"
+ mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
+ 
+ TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
+ LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/lix-install-${TIMESTAMP}.log"
+ STATE_BEFORE="${LOG_DIR}/system-state-before-${TIMESTAMP}.txt"
+ STATE_AFTER="${LOG_DIR}/system-state-after-${TIMESTAMP}.txt"
+ NIX_STORY="${LOG_DIR}/nix-story-${TIMESTAMP}.md"
+ 
+ # Function to log with timestamp
+ log() {
+     echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ }
+ 
+ # Function to capture system state
+ capture_system_state() {
+     local output_file="$1"
+     {
+         echo "=== System State Capture - $(date) ==="
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Disk Usage ---"
+         df -h | grep -E "(Filesystem|/nix|/$)"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Nix Directories ---"
+         ls -lah /nix 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "/nix does not exist"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Nix Config ---"
+         cat /etc/nix/nix.conf 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "/etc/nix/nix.conf does not exist"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Nix Users/Groups ---"
+         dscl . -list /Users | grep nix || echo "No nix users"
+         dscl . -list /Groups | grep nix || echo "No nix groups"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- LaunchDaemons/LaunchAgents ---"
+         ls -lah /Library/LaunchDaemons/org.nixos.* 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "No Nix launch daemons"
+         ls -lah ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.nixos.* 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "No Nix launch agents"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Shell Profiles ---"
+         grep -n "nix" ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "No Nix in shell profiles"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Environment Variables ---"
+         env | grep -i nix || echo "No NIX_* environment variables"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- Processes ---"
+         ps aux | grep -i nix | grep -v grep || echo "No Nix processes running"
+         echo ""
+         echo "--- APFS Volumes ---"
+         diskutil list | grep -i nix || echo "No Nix APFS volumes"
+         echo ""
+     } &gt; "$output_file" 2&gt;&amp;1
+ }
+ 
+ log "=========================================="
+ log "Lix Full Installation with Logging"
+ log "Timestamp: $TIMESTAMP"
+ log "=========================================="
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Capture system state BEFORE installation
+ log "Capturing system state BEFORE installation..."
+ capture_system_state "$STATE_BEFORE"
+ log "Pre-installation state saved to: $STATE_BEFORE"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Check if Nix is already installed
+ if [ -d "/nix" ] &amp;&amp; [ -f "/etc/nix/nix.conf" ]; then
+     log "WARNING: Nix appears to be already installed!"
+     log "Checking current installation..."
+     if command -v nix &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+         log "Nix version: $(nix --version 2&gt;&amp;1 || echo 'unknown')"
+         read -p "Continue anyway? This may reinstall. [y/N] " -n 1 -r
+         echo
+         if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
+             log "Installation cancelled"
+             exit 0
+         fi
+     fi
+ fi
+ 
+ log "Starting Lix installation..."
+ log "This will:"
+ log "  1. Answer 'e' (explain) to see what will happen"
+ log "  2. Then answer 'Y' (yes) to proceed"
+ log "  3. Log everything to: $LOG_FILE"
+ log ""
+ log "You will be prompted for your sudo password"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Create a script that answers: explain, then yes
+ INSTALL_SCRIPT=$(mktemp)
+ cat &gt; "$INSTALL_SCRIPT" &lt;&lt; 'INSTALL_EOF'
+ #!/usr/bin/env bash
+ # Automated responses for Lix installer
+ 
+ # Wait for "Enable flakes?" prompt and answer Y
+ expect_prompt() {
+     while IFS= read -r line; do
+         echo "$line" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+         if echo "$line" | grep -q "Enable flakes"; then
+             echo "Y" &gt;&amp;2
+             echo "Y"
+         elif echo "$line" | grep -q "Proceed.*\\[Y\\]es"; then
+             # First answer 'e' for explain, then 'Y' for yes
+             echo "e" &gt;&amp;2
+             echo "e"
+             sleep 2
+             echo "Y" &gt;&amp;2
+             echo "Y"
+         fi
+     done
+ }
+ 
+ curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | \
+ sh -s -- install 2&gt;&amp;1 | expect_prompt
+ INSTALL_EOF
+ 
+ chmod +x "$INSTALL_SCRIPT"
+ 
+ # Actually, let's use a simpler approach with expect or a here-doc
+ # Since we need to handle "explain" then "Y", let's use expect properly
+ 
+ log "Running installer with automated responses..."
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Use expect to handle: Enable flakes? -&gt; Y, Proceed? -&gt; e (explain), then Y (yes)
+ expect &lt;&lt; EXPECT_SCRIPT 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ set timeout 600
+ set log_file [open "$LOG_FILE" a]
+ 
+ spawn bash -c "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install"
+ 
+ log_user 1
+ 
+ expect {
+     -re "Enable flakes\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+         puts $log_file "[AUTO] Answering 'Y' to enable flakes"
+         send "Y\r"
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "Proceed\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+         puts $log_file "[AUTO] Answering 'e' for explain, then 'Y' to proceed"
+         send "e\r"
+         expect {
+             -re ".*" {
+                 # Read the explanation
+                 exp_continue
+             }
+             -re "Proceed\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+                 send "Y\r"
+                 exp_continue
+             }
+         }
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "(Password|password):" {
+         puts $log_file "[PROMPT] Sudo password required"
+         interact {
+             \r { send "\r" }
+         }
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     timeout {
+         puts $log_file "[ERROR] Timeout"
+         exit 1
+     }
+     eof {
+         puts $log_file "[SUCCESS] Installation complete"
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ close $log_file
+ EXPECT_SCRIPT
+ 
+ INSTALL_EXIT=$?
+ 
+ log ""
+ log "=========================================="
+ if [ $INSTALL_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
+     log "✓ Installation completed successfully!"
+ else
+     log "⚠ Installation exited with code: $INSTALL_EXIT"
+ fi
+ log "=========================================="
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Capture system state AFTER installation
+ log "Capturing system state AFTER installation..."
+ sleep 2  # Give system a moment to settle
+ capture_system_state "$STATE_AFTER"
+ log "Post-installation state saved to: $STATE_AFTER"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Generate Nix Story document
+ log "Generating Nix Story document..."
+ cat &gt; "$NIX_STORY" &lt;&lt; STORY_EOF
+ # Nix Installation Story
+ 
+ **Installation Date**: $(date)
+ **Timestamp**: $TIMESTAMP
+ **Installer**: Lix (Nix fork)
+ 
+ ## Installation Summary
+ 
+ $(if [ $INSTALL_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then echo "✅ Installation completed successfully"; else echo "⚠️ Installation completed with exit code: $INSTALL_EXIT"; fi)
+ 
+ ## Files Generated
+ 
+ - **Installation Log**: \&#96;$LOG_FILE\&#96;
+ - **Pre-Installation State**: \&#96;$STATE_BEFORE\&#96;
+ - **Post-Installation State**: \&#96;$STATE_AFTER\&#96;
+ - **This Story**: \&#96;$NIX_STORY\&#96;
+ 
+ ## What Changed
+ 
+ ### Before Installation
+ 
+ \&#96;\&#96;\&#96;
+ $(head -50 "$STATE_BEFORE")
+ \&#96;\&#96;\&#96;
+ 
+ ### After Installation
+ 
+ \&#96;\&#96;\&#96;
+ $(head -50 "$STATE_AFTER")
+ \&#96;\&#96;\&#96;
+ 
+ ## Installation Log
+ 
+ \&#96;\&#96;\&#96;
+ $(tail -100 "$LOG_FILE")
+ \&#96;\&#96;\&#96;
+ 
+ ## Key Changes Made
+ 
+ ### 1. Nix Store Location
+ $(if [ -d "/nix" ]; then
+     echo "- Created: \&#96;/nix\&#96; directory"
+     echo "- Type: $(diskutil info /nix 2&gt;/dev/null | grep "File System" || echo "APFS volume")"
+     echo "- Size: $(df -h /nix 2&gt;/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $2 " total, " $4 " available"}')"
+ else
+     echo "- \&#96;/nix\&#96; directory not found (installation may have failed)"
+ fi)
+ 
+ ### 2. Configuration Files
+ $(if [ -f "/etc/nix/nix.conf" ]; then
+     echo "- Created: \&#96;/etc/nix/nix.conf\&#96;"
+     echo ""
+     echo "Contents:"
+     echo "\&#96;\&#96;\&#96;"
+     cat /etc/nix/nix.conf
+     echo "\&#96;\&#96;\&#96;"
+ else
+     echo "- \&#96;/etc/nix/nix.conf\&#96; not found"
+ fi)
+ 
+ ### 3. System Users/Groups
+ $(if dscl . -list /Users | grep -q nix; then
+     echo "- Created Nix build users:"
+     dscl . -list /Users | grep nix | sed 's/^/  - /'
+ else
+     echo "- No Nix users found"
+ fi)
+ 
+ $(if dscl . -list /Groups | grep -q nix; then
+     echo "- Created Nix groups:"
+     dscl . -list /Groups | grep nix | sed 's/^/  - /'
+ else
+     echo "- No Nix groups found"
+ fi)
+

+ $(if [ -f "/Library/LaunchDaemons/org.nixos.nix-daemon.plist" ]; then

+     echo "- Location: \&#96;/Library/LaunchDaemons/org.nixos.nix-daemon.plist\&#96;"

+

+ $(if grep -q nix ~/.zshrc 2&gt;/dev/null || grep -q nix ~/.zprofile 2&gt;/dev/null; then

+         if [ -f "$file" ] &amp;&amp; grep -q nix "$file" 2&gt;/dev/null; then
+             echo "$file:"
+             grep -n nix "$file" | head -5
+         fi
+     done
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- APFS Volumes ---"
+     diskutil list | grep -i nix || echo "No Nix APFS volumes"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Environment Variables ---"
+     env | grep -i nix || echo "No NIX_* variables"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Processes ---"
+     ps aux | grep -i nix | grep -v grep || echo "No Nix processes"
+ } &gt; "$STATE_BEFORE" 2&gt;&amp;1
+ log "Pre-installation state saved to: $STATE_BEFORE"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Check if already installed
+ if [ -f "/nix/receipt.json" ]; then
+     log "⚠️  Found existing Nix installation receipt"
+     log "Checking if Nix is functional..."
+     if command -v nix &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+         NIX_VERSION=$(nix --version 2&gt;&amp;1 || echo "unknown")
+         log "Nix appears to be installed: $NIX_VERSION"
+         log ""
+         read -p "Nix seems to be installed. Reinstall anyway? [y/N] " -n 1 -r
+         echo
+         if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
+             log "Skipping installation. Nix is already installed."
+             log "To reinstall, run: /nix/nix-installer uninstall"
+             exit 0
+         fi
+         log "Proceeding with reinstallation..."
+     else
+         log "Receipt found but Nix command not available. Proceeding with installation..."
+     fi
+ fi
+ 
+ log "Starting Lix installation..."
+ log "Strategy: Answer 'e' (explain) then 'Y' (yes) to all prompts"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Create expect script for automated installation
+ EXPECT_SCRIPT=$(mktemp)
+ cat &gt; "$EXPECT_SCRIPT" &lt;&lt; 'EXPECT_EOF'
+ #!/usr/bin/expect -f
+ 
+ set timeout 600
+ set log_file [open "$env(LOG_FILE)" a]
+ 
+ # Spawn the installer
+ spawn bash -c "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.lix.systems/lix | sh -s -- install"
+ 
+ # Enable logging
+ log_user 1
+ 
+ # Handle prompts
+ expect {
+     -re "Enable flakes\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+         puts $log_file "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [AUTO] Answering 'Y' to enable flakes"
+         send "Y\r"
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "Proceed\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+         puts $log_file "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [AUTO] Answering 'e' for explanation"
+         send "e\r"
+         
+         # Wait for explanation to finish, then answer Y
+         expect {
+             -re "Proceed\\?.*\\[Y\\]es.*:" {
+                 puts $log_file "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [AUTO] Answering 'Y' to proceed after explanation"
+                 send "Y\r"
+                 exp_continue
+             }
+             timeout {
+                 # If no proceed prompt appears, continue
+                 exp_continue
+             }
+         }
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     -re "(Password|password|sudo.*password):" {
+         puts $log_file "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [PROMPT] Sudo password required - waiting for user input"
+         interact {
+             \r { send "\r" }
+         }
+         exp_continue
+     }
+     timeout {
+         puts $log_file "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [ERROR] Timeout waiting for prompt"
+         exit 1
+     }
+     eof {
+         puts $log_file "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [SUCCESS] Installation process completed"
+         close $log_file
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ wait
+ close $log_file
+ EXPECT_EOF
+ 
+ chmod +x "$EXPECT_SCRIPT"
+ 
+ # Export LOG_FILE for expect script
+ export LOG_FILE
+ 
+ log "Running installer with expect automation..."
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Run expect script
+ expect -f "$EXPECT_SCRIPT" 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
+ 
+ INSTALL_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
+ 
+ # Clean up
+ rm -f "$EXPECT_SCRIPT"
+ 
+ log ""
+ log "=========================================="
+ if [ $INSTALL_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
+     log "✓ Installation process completed!"
+ else
+     log "⚠ Installation exited with code: $INSTALL_EXIT"
+ fi
+ log "=========================================="
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Wait a moment for system to settle
+ sleep 3
+ 
+ # Capture system state AFTER
+ log "Capturing POST-installation system state..."
+ {
+     echo "=== POST-INSTALLATION SYSTEM STATE ==="
+     echo "Date: $(date)"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Nix Installation Check ---"
+     command -v nix &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1 &amp;&amp; echo "Nix command: $(nix --version 2&gt;&amp;1)" || echo "Nix command: NOT FOUND"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- /nix Directory ---"
+     if [ -d "/nix" ]; then
+         ls -lah /nix | head -20
+         echo ""
+         echo "Disk usage:"
+         df -h /nix 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "Cannot get disk usage"
+         echo ""
+         echo "Store contents (first 10 items):"
+         ls /nix/store 2&gt;/dev/null | head -10 || echo "Store empty or inaccessible"
+     else
+         echo "/nix does not exist"
+     fi
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- /etc/nix Configuration ---"
+     if [ -d "/etc/nix" ]; then
+         ls -lah /etc/nix
+         [ -f "/etc/nix/nix.conf" ] &amp;&amp; echo "" &amp;&amp; echo "nix.conf contents:" &amp;&amp; cat /etc/nix/nix.conf
+     else
+         echo "/etc/nix does not exist"
+     fi
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Nix Receipt ---"
+     [ -f "/nix/receipt.json" ] &amp;&amp; cat /nix/receipt.json || echo "No receipt.json found"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Nix Users ---"
+     dscl . -list /Users | grep -E "^nix" || echo "No nix users"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Nix Groups ---"
+     dscl . -list /Groups | grep -E "^nix" || echo "No nix groups"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Launch Services ---"
+     ls -lah /Library/LaunchDaemons/org.nixos.* 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "No Nix launch daemons"
+     ls -lah ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.nixos.* 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "No Nix launch agents"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Launch Service Status ---"
+     launchctl list | grep nix || echo "No Nix services running"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Shell Profile Nix References ---"
+     for file in ~/.zshrc ~/.zprofile ~/.zshenv ~/.bashrc ~/.bash_profile; do
+         if [ -f "$file" ] &amp;&amp; grep -q nix "$file" 2&gt;/dev/null; then
+             echo "$file:"
+             grep -n nix "$file" | head -5
+         fi
+     done
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- APFS Volumes ---"
+     diskutil list | grep -i nix || echo "No Nix APFS volumes"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Nix Profile ---"
+     [ -d "$HOME/.nix-profile" ] &amp;&amp; ls -lah "$HOME/.nix-profile" | head -10 || echo "No ~/.nix-profile"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Environment Variables ---"
+     env | grep -i nix || echo "No NIX_* variables"
+     echo ""
+     echo "--- Processes ---"
+     ps aux | grep -i nix | grep -v grep || echo "No Nix processes"
+ } &gt; "$STATE_AFTER" 2&gt;&amp;1
+ log "Post-installation state saved to: $STATE_AFTER"
+ log ""
+ 
+ # Generate comprehensive Nix Story
+ log "Generating comprehensive Nix Story document..."
+ 
+ # Calculate differences
+ DIFF_OUTPUT=$(diff -u "$STATE_BEFORE" "$STATE_AFTER" 2&gt;&amp;1 || true)

+ cat &gt; "$NIX_STORY" &lt;&lt; STORY_EOF

+ 
+ **Installation Date**: $(date)
+ **Timestamp**: $TIMESTAMP
+ **Installer**: Lix (Nix fork v2.94.0)
+ **Installation Method**: Automated with explain-then-yes responses
+ 
+ ## Executive Summary
+ 
+ $(if [ $INSTALL_EXIT -eq 0 ]; then 
+     echo "✅ **Installation Status**: Completed successfully"
+     if command -v nix &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then

+     else

+ 
+ ## Installation Process

+ ### Automated Responses

+ 1. **Enable flakes?** → Answered **Y** (Yes)

+ ### Installation Plan (What Was Explained)

+ $(head -100 "$STATE_BEFORE")

```
# Run Lix Installer - Complete with Logging

## Quick Command

Run this in **your own terminal** (not Cursor's agent terminal):

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash
cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config &amp;&amp; ./install-lix-complete.sh
&#96;&#96;&#96;

## What It Does

1. ✅ **Captures system state BEFORE** installation
2. ✅ **Runs installer** with automated responses:
   - Answers "Y" to "Enable flakes?"
   - Answers "e" (explain) then "Y" (yes) to "Proceed?"
3. ✅ **Logs everything** to &#96;logs/lix-install-TIMESTAMP.log&#96;
4. ✅ **Captures system state AFTER** installation
5. ✅ **Generates comprehensive "Nix Story"** document

## What You'll See

1. System state capture (pre-installation)
2. Installer starts downloading
3. Prompt: "Enable flakes? ([Y]es/[n]o):" → Auto-answers Y
4. Prompt: "Proceed? ([Y]es/[n]o/[e]xplain):" → Auto-answers e (explain)
5. Explanation of what will happen
6. Prompt again: "Proceed? ([Y]es/[n]o/[e]xplain):" → Auto-answers Y
7. **You'll be prompted for sudo password** → Type it in
8. Installation proceeds
9. System state capture (post-installation)
10. Nix Story document generated

## Generated Files

After installation, check:

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash
# View the Nix Story (comprehensive documentation)
cat logs/nix-story-*.md

# View installation log
tail -f logs/lix-install-*.log

# Compare before/after
diff logs/system-state-before-*.txt logs/system-state-after-*.txt
&#96;&#96;&#96;

## Latest Files

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash
# Get the latest files
LATEST_LOG=$(ls -t logs/lix-install-*.log | head -1)
LATEST_STORY=$(ls -t logs/nix-story-*.md | head -1)
LATEST_BEFORE=$(ls -t logs/system-state-before-*.txt | head -1)
LATEST_AFTER=$(ls -t logs/system-state-after-*.txt | head -1)

echo "Log: $LATEST_LOG"
echo "Story: $LATEST_STORY"
echo "Before: $LATEST_BEFORE"
echo "After: $LATEST_AFTER"
&#96;&#96;&#96;


```
</details>
</tool-use>

---



---


## Ready to run

**Command to run in your terminal:**

```bash
cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config && ./install-lix-complete.sh
```

## What it does

1. Captures system state before installation
2. Runs installer with automated responses:
   - "Enable flakes?" → **Y**
   - "Proceed?" → **e** (explain), then **Y** (yes)
3. Logs everything to `logs/lix-install-TIMESTAMP.log`
4. Captures system state after installation
5. Generates a "Nix Story" document with:
   - What changed
   - Before/after comparison
   - Installation log excerpts
   - Verification steps
   - Troubleshooting guide

## Generated files

After installation, you'll have:
- `logs/lix-install-TIMESTAMP.log` - Full installation log
- `logs/system-state-before-TIMESTAMP.txt` - Pre-installation state
- `logs/system-state-after-TIMESTAMP.txt` - Post-installation state
- `logs/nix-story-TIMESTAMP.md` - Complete "Nix Story" narrative

## View the story

After installation:

```bash
# View the latest Nix Story
cat logs/nix-story-*.md | less

# Or find the latest
LATEST=$(ls -t logs/nix-story-*.md | head -1)
cat "$LATEST"
```

The script is ready. Run it in your terminal and enter your sudo password when prompted. It will handle the rest and generate the documentation.

```
# 🚀 Install Nix Now - Episode Tracking Enabled

## Quick Start

**Run this in YOUR terminal** (not Cursor's agent):

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash
cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config &amp;&amp; ./install-lix-complete.sh
&#96;&#96;&#96;

## What's New

✅ **Episode Tracking**: Each installation attempt is tracked as an episode  
✅ **System Notifications**: You'll get a macOS notification when sudo password is needed  
✅ **Master Story**: All episodes are appended to &#96;logs/nix-story-complete.md&#96;  
✅ **Individual Episodes**: Each episode also saved separately with timestamp  

## What Happens

1. **Pre-installation state** captured
2. **Installer runs** with automated responses:
   - "Enable flakes?" → **Y**
   - "Proceed?" → **e** (explain), then **Y** (yes)
3. **🔔 Notification appears** when sudo password is needed
4. **You type password** in terminal
5. **Installation proceeds**
6. **Post-installation state** captured
7. **Episode story** generated and appended to master story

## Generated Files

After installation:

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash
# View the latest episode
cat logs/nix-story-*.md | tail -1 | head -1 | xargs cat

# View ALL episodes (complete story)
cat logs/nix-story-complete.md

# View installation log
tail -f logs/lix-install-*.log
&#96;&#96;&#96;

## Branch &amp; Fork

- **Branch**: &#96;nixstory&#96; 
- **Fork**: &#96;aculich/nixos-config-2026&#96;
- **Status**: All changes pushed to fork

## Next Steps After Installation

&#96;&#96;&#96;bash
# Activate Nix in current shell
source ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh

# Verify installation
nix --version

# Test the configuration
cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config
nix run .#build
&#96;&#96;&#96;


```
</details>
</tool-use>

## Setup complete

### What's been done

1. Created `nixstory` branch
2. Created fork: `aculich/nixos-config-2026`
3. Pushed all changes to the fork
4. Enhanced installer with:
   - Episode tracking (each install is an episode)
   - macOS notification when sudo password is needed
   - Master story file that appends all episodes
   - Individual episode files with timestamps

### Run the installer

Run this in your terminal (not Cursor's agent):

```bash
cd /Users/me/toolchain-2026/nixos-config && ./install-lix-complete.sh
```

### What to expect

1. Pre-installation state captured
2. Installer starts (auto-answers Y to flakes, e then Y to proceed)
3. macOS notification appears when sudo password is needed
4. Type your password in the terminal
5. Installation completes
6. Episode story generated and appended to master story

### Generated files

- `logs/lix-install-TIMESTAMP.log` - Full installation log
- `logs/nix-story-TIMESTAMP.md` - Individual episode
- `logs/nix-story-complete.md` - Master story (all episodes appended)
- `logs/system-state-before-TIMESTAMP.txt` - Pre-install state
- `logs/system-state-after-TIMESTAMP.txt` - Post-install state

### View the story

After installation:

```bash
# View all episodes (complete story)
cat logs/nix-story-complete.md

# View latest episode
ls -t logs/nix-story-*.md | head -1 | xargs cat
```

Everything is committed and pushed to `aculich/nixos-config-2026` on the `nixstory` branch. Run the installer when ready; you'll get a notification when the password is needed.
